finding: Implementation: top-N=1000 most-frequent bigrams (deterministic sort by (-count, token-id) for tie-breaking), Hermitian PSD Laplacian over bigram-token nodes with adjacency window=1 (immediately-following bigrams), eigendecompose via numpy.linalg.eigh (Julia driver written for bit-exact when Julia present; Python reference run because Julia is not installed in WSL2 — install requirement documented in .md). State vector per chunk = L¹-normalised bigram frequency over top-N alphabet. Project state onto eigenbasis: coeffs = V^T · state. Similarity = cosine on real-coefficient vectors. Cohen's d on per-chunk similarity arrays.

finding: Bigram refinement DISCRIMINATES random_baseline strongly but is NULL for surface mutations. Cohen's d: attested_held_out vs citation_swap=+0.0019 [NULL], value_mutation=-0.0004 [NULL], vocab_swap=+0.0361 [NULL], random_baseline=+3.8842 [DISCRIMINATES]. Per-class real_sim_mean: attested_held_out=0.8776, citation_swap=0.8775, value_mutation=0.8776, vocab_swap=0.8755, random_baseline=0.6921. Bit-exact reproducibility confirmed across two consecutive runs (Cohen's d identical, class_sim_means identical).

Why bigram catches random_baseline: character-shuffle destroys bigram co-occurrence completely — the shuffled text has approximately uniform random bigram distribution, which has very different spectral projection onto the corpus-specific bigram Laplacian eigenbasis than attested ordered text. Cohen's d ~4 reflects this large structural gap. Why bigram MISSES surface mutations: citation_swap / value_mutation / vocab_swap only mutate small numbers of tokens in each chunk (e.g., 1-3 arXiv IDs, ~7 value patterns, ~9 vocab patterns). The bulk of the chunk's 2000 characters generates ~1999 bigrams of which the vast majority are unchanged. Bigram-frequency vectors are nearly identical → fingerprints nearly identical → Cohen's d ≈ 0. The signal-to-noise ratio of these surface mutations against a 1000-dim bigram-frequency vector is too low.

This result reveals a USEFUL stratification: bigram-cascade reliably detects CASCADE-STRUCTURE-DESTRUCTION (shuffle, machine-generated random-token output, certain truncation/repetition failure modes) but NOT TOKEN-LEVEL SURFACE EDITS (citation hallucination, value swap, vocab swap). The two failure modes are detected by DIFFERENT mechanisms. Cascade-shape detection (which is what the framework predicts) IS empirically real at bigram order — random_baseline d ~4 confirms it. Citation/value/vocab discrimination requires a separate mechanism (e.g., per-token validity check, NER + database lookup, value-domain consistency) — these are NOT cascade-shape failures and shouldn't be expected to fall out of a cascade-shape detector.

Bigram-cascade detector runtime: 1000-node Laplacian eigendecompose = 1.24s one-time (cacheable); per-chunk projection = ~1.35 us/char (2000-char chunks). Same order of magnitude as parent unigram detector. n=1000 stays within srmech.amsc.laplacian's 256-node native bound only if we sparse-truncate (Class K top-k modes); full 1000-dim native port would need a separate path. Per-chunk steady-state cost remains well under Spike #122's 44 us/token budget.

finding: Bigram bounds the framework's resolution at the cascade-structure-destruction level. To detect surface-level mutations the detector must compose with: (a) trigram / higher-order n-gram (may improve vocab_swap detection where multi-token phrases mutate), (b) per-token validity Layer 2 (e.g., arXiv-ID regex + DOI resolver — catches citation hallucination directly without spectral analysis), (c) value-domain consistency Layer 3 (semantic-domain-knowledge check — catches value_mutation but requires domain knowledge), (d) subword tokenisation BPE-style which may interpolate the trigram vs bigram tradeoff. The three-layer hallucination protocol per [[feedback_hallucination_detection_three_layer_protocol]] survives: bigram-cascade IS the Layer 1 cascade-shape check; Layer 2/3 remain separate concerns.

Math-doesn't-lie discipline (per [[feedback_every_doc_edit_faces_falsification]]) returned an honest stratified result: bigram catches structural destruction (real positive finding), bigram misses surface mutations (negative within scope; orthogonal mechanism needed). Both findings shipped together with mechanism diagnosis. Bit-exact reproducibility (Python-side; Julia driver written but Julia not installed) confirmed across two runs. Framework hypothesis stratified rather than confirmed/falsified wholesale — useful refinement.

anchor_class: L+I (cascade) confirmed; Layer 2/3 (token-validity) needed for surface mutations

finding: Conductor decisions: (a) bigram-cascade is the canonical Layer 1 cascade-shape detector — flag for native-srmech port consideration with Class K top-k truncation to stay within the n≤256 native bound; (b) DO NOT advertise bigram-cascade as a citation/value/vocab hallucination detector — that's a category error; bigram catches CASCADE-STRUCTURE-DESTRUCTION which is a different failure mode; (c) Layer 2 (citation regex + DOI resolver) and Layer 3 (value-domain consistency) need their own implementation paths — not derivable from bigram-spectral. (d) Open follow-up: should trigram or BPE-subword be tried next? Trigram is a natural extension (top-N over 64³ = 262144 trigrams; n=1000 still bounded). However, evidence suggests surface mutations may resist any pure n-gram detector at reasonable n because the mutation rate per chunk is too low to perturb the n-gram distribution materially. Recommend stopping the n-gram refinement arc here and treating Layer 2/3 as separate engineering work — n-gram only addresses cascade-structure-destruction, which bigram already handles well.
